evidence.title: About Copilot cloud agent
evidence.finding: Cloud agent uses ephemeral Actions environment, supports issue assignment and staged plan-to-PR work; integration parity differs.

evidence.title: GitHub Copilot
evidence.finding: Family product page retrieved; no assumption of identical CLI, app and editor capabilities.

evidence.title: Copilot in the cloud
evidence.locator: Environment comparison; ways to work; limitations
evidence.finding: GitHub distinguishes cloud sandboxes from Actions-based sessions, including repository scope, compute controls, shared logs and a 59-minute Actions limit.

evidence.title: GitHub Copilot CLI
evidence.locator: Supported OS; modes; sandboxing; GitHub tasks
evidence.finding: The CLI runs interactively or by prompt, supports local/cloud sandbox modes and structured planning, and can act on GitHub issues and PRs.

evidence.title: Plans for GitHub Copilot
evidence.locator: Plan overview; individual plans; credit allowances
evidence.finding: The current plan table uses GitHub AI credits and separates free chat/client access from paid cloud work.

evidence.title: GitHub Copilot app
evidence.finding: Copilot app supports macOS, Linux and Windows, separate worktrees/branches, parallel sessions and PR review/merge workflows. Organization policy governs access.

evidence.title: GitHub Mobile
evidence.finding: GitHub Mobile ships Android and iOS apps and supports Copilot chat and assigning issues to Copilot.

evidence.title: Cloud sandboxes
evidence.finding: Cloud sandboxes run isolated Linux sessions without needing the client connected. Multiple sessions run in parallel; stopped sessions retain snapshots and resume files. GitHub Actions remains a separate environment option.

evidence.title: Creating a custom environment
evidence.finding: Users can register a Linux host or codespace as a custom execution environment. The user operates the host, workspace and dependencies. Closing a client does not stop the machine.

evidence.title: Delegating and parallelizing
evidence.finding: /fleet makes the main agent orchestrate subtasks and dependencies, run independent children concurrently and combine results. Each child uses its own context and additional model usage.

evidence.title: Copilot App projects
evidence.finding: Projects retain ongoing goals, conversations, artifacts and recurring work. Overview groups Needs input, Open, Working and Done. Users inspect plans, changes and PRs and steer sessions.

evidence.title: Copilot automations
evidence.finding: Paid-plan automations trigger on schedules, repository events or API requests. Per-run credit controls and repository write scope are configurable; shared automation visibility/editing follows repository permissions.

evidence.title: Copilot issue creation and updates
evidence.finding: In public preview, Copilot creates or updates GitHub issues from prompts/images, including title, body, labels and assignees. Humans review drafts before submission.

evidence.title: Third-party coding agents
evidence.finding: Paid Copilot plans support public-preview Claude Agent SDK and Codex SDK coding agents. These are named coding-agent integrations, not only models. GitHub policy must enable each partner separately.

evidence.title: Copilot CLI Authentication
evidence.locator: Unauthenticated use; Offline mode; OAuth SSO
evidence.finding: BYOK requires no GitHub account. COPILOT_OFFLINE=true avoids GitHub services and fully disables telemetry; only the configured provider remains. Complete airgap requires a local/in-network model. OAuth can authorize SAML organizations.

evidence.title: Agent management for enterprises
evidence.finding: Enterprise owners, AI managers and organization owners control Copilot and partner-agent policies at different scopes. Enterprise audit logs can track agentic activity; partner policies are separate from Copilot.

evidence.title: Additional Product Terms
evidence.finding: Copilot use is governed by GitHub Generative AI Services Terms for direct Business/Enterprise purchases, Microsoft Product Terms for Microsoft purchases, or GitHub Terms AI section otherwise.

evidence.title: Copilot connectors
evidence.finding: Copilot in the cloud can use connected tools from a mobile browser, as well as GitHub Mobile on iOS and Android.

evidence.title: Building a secure cloud environment for agents
evidence.finding: GitHub recommends hosted runners so each cloud-agent Actions job runs on a fresh virtual machine; self-hosted runners remain an alternative.

evidence.title: Troubleshooting Copilot cloud agent
evidence.locator: Copilot will not respond to my pull request comments
evidence.finding: Copilot accepts @copilot comments on its assigned open PRs from people with repository write access; it uses those comments to continue work. This is shared PR prompting, distinct from view-only local-session sharing.

evidence.title: Billing for cloud and local sandboxes
evidence.locator: How sandbox usage is measured; Pricing
evidence.finding: Cloud sandbox compute, memory and snapshot storage are metered. After the shared compute allowance, additional use is billed. Published rates are $0.000024 per compute second, $0.000003 per GiB-second and $0.005 per GiB-month.

evidence.title: Authenticating GitHub Copilot CLI
evidence.finding: Copilot CLI can connect to a user-provided model provider API key without GitHub authentication; GitHub-hosted features still require GitHub authentication.
